Voat has a spam problem. This should not come as a surprise to users who've been here for more than a day. The problem is most easily seen in unmoderated @system subs (/v/whatever, /v/AskVoat, /v/science). There's little doubt that it annoys users and moderators, and it may even turn away new users and prevent recruitment. How to deal with it is a question of both politics and technical know how. Given my lack of expertise on this issue, I've chosen to ask questions in the hope that others can contribute their ideas in this thread.

##What is Spam?

A critical issue on voat is that spam is not defined in the user agreement, which only states that, "You may not post any graphics, text, photographs, images, video, audio or other material that we deem to be junk or spam." This leaves moderators to subjectively determine what constitutes spam, and gives the adminstration free range to delete whatever they want. We need a clear, unambiguous definition in order to deal with the problem without infringing on user rights.

##What Makes a User a Spammer?

There's also the need to determine when a user should be banned for advertising on voat. Should a user be punished for, say, promoting their artwork, while also contributing to the community as a typical user? I've heard that the administration allows a user to advertise in 20% of their posts, though it is not outlined in the user agreement. Is this good enough for the users?

##Should unmoderated (@system) subs exist?

Currently, I'm aware of three subverses that completely lack moderation: /v/whatever, /v/AskVoat, and /v/science. As a consequence, spammers have free range of these subverses. Is that acceptable? Does the threat of rogue moderators really outweigh the negative effects that spam had on these subverses and voat as a whole, or does this lack of moderation make voat more insecure?

##Can we do better to block spam?

Currently, the admins have put in place several technical measures to prevent spam. They block domains that spam, they restrict new user's downvoting privileges, and they restrict users posting privileges when their CCP dips into the negatives. They have also implemented a "report spam" button that directs moderators to the post in question.

I have a genuine concern about restricting user's speech when they dip into negative CCP. This can be easily gamed to effectively silence dissent. But what other technical solutions could we develop to combat spam?
